202: 	src, err := ioutil.ReadAll(r)
203: 	if err != nil {
204: 		diags = diags.Append(fmt.Errorf("Failed to read %s", path))
205: 		return diags
206: 	}
207: 
208: 	// Register this path as a synthetic configuration source, so that any
209: 	// diagnostic errors can include the source code snippet
210: 	c.registerSynthConfigSource(path, src)
211: 
212: 	// File must be parseable as HCL native syntax before we'll try to format
213: 	// it. If not, the formatter is likely to make drastic changes that would
214: 	// be hard for the user to undo.
215: 	_, syntaxDiags := hclsyntax.ParseConfig(src, path, hcl.Pos{Line: 1, Column: 1})
216: 	if syntaxDiags.HasErrors() {
217: 		diags = diags.Append(syntaxDiags)
218: 		return diags
219: 	}
220: 
221: 	result := c.formatSourceCode(src, path)
222: 
223: 	if !bytes.Equal(src, result) {
224: 		// Something was changed
225: 		if c.list {
226: 			fmt.Fprintln(w, path)
227: 		}
228: 		if c.write {
229: 			err := ioutil.WriteFile(path, result, 0644)
230: 			if err != nil {
231: 				diags = diags.Append(fmt.Errorf("Failed to write %s", path))
232: 				return diags
233: 			}
234: 		}
235: 		if c.diff {
236: 			diff, err := c.bytesDiff(src, result, path)
237: 			if err != nil {
238: 				diags = diags.Append(fmt.Errorf("Failed to generate diff for %s: %s", path, err))
239: 				return diags
240: 			}
241: 			w.Write(diff)
242: 		}
243: 	}
244: 
245: 	if !c.list && !c.write && !c.diff {
246: 		_, err = w.Write(result)
247: 		if err != nil {
248: 			diags = diags.Append(fmt.Errorf("Failed to write result"))
249: 		}
250: 	}
251: 
252: 	return diags
253: }

255: func (c *FmtCommand) processDir(path string, stdout io.Writer) tfdiags.Diagnostics {
256: 	var diags tfdiags.Diagnostics
257: 
258: 	log.Printf("[TRACE] terraform fmt: looking for files in %s", path)
259: 
260: 	entries, err := ioutil.ReadDir(path)
261: 	if err != nil {
262: 		switch {
263: 		case os.IsNotExist(err):
264: 			diags = diags.Append(fmt.Errorf("There is no configuration directory at %s", path))
265: 		default:
266: 			// ReadDir does not produce error messages that are end-user-appropriate,
267: 			// so we'll need to simplify here.
268: 			diags = diags.Append(fmt.Errorf("Cannot read directory %s", path))
269: 		}
270: 		return diags
271: 	}
272: 
273: 	for _, info := range entries {
274: 		name := info.Name()
275: 		if c.shouldIgnoreFile(name) {
276: 			continue
277: 		}
278: 		subPath := filepath.Join(path, name)
279: 		if info.IsDir() {
280: 			if c.recursive {
281: 				subDiags := c.processDir(subPath, stdout)
282: 				diags = diags.Append(subDiags)
283: 			}
284: 
285: 			// We do not recurse into child directories by default because we
286: 			// want to mimic the file-reading behavior of "terraform plan", etc,
287: 			// operating on one module at a time.
288: 			continue
289: 		}
290: 
291: 		if !c.classifyFormatPath(name) {
292: 			continue
293: 		}
294: 		f, err := os.Open(subPath)
295: 		if err != nil {
296: 			// Open does not produce error messages that are end-user-appropriate,
297: 			// so we'll need to simplify here.
298: 			diags = diags.Append(fmt.Errorf("Failed to read file %s", subPath))
299: 			continue
300: 		}
301: 
302: 		fileDiags := c.processFile(c.normalizePath(subPath), f, stdout, false)
303: 		diags = diags.Append(fileDiags)
304: 		f.Close()
305: 	}
306: 
307: 	return diags
308: }

311: // is selected (directly or indirectly) on the command line.
312: func (c *FmtCommand) formatSourceCode(src []byte, filename string) []byte {
313: 	f, diags := hclwrite.ParseConfig(src, filename, hcl.InitialPos)
314: 	if diags.HasErrors() {
315: 		// It would be weird to get here because the caller should already have
316: 		// checked for syntax errors and returned them. We'll just do nothing
317: 		// in this case, returning the input exactly as given.
318: 		return src
319: 	}
320: 
321: 	c.formatBody(f.Body(), nil)
322: 
323: 	result := f.Bytes()
324: 	c.lastFormatResult = result
325: 	c.formatVisitCount++
326: 	return result
327: }

329: func (c *FmtCommand) formatBody(body *hclwrite.Body, inBlocks []string) {
330: 	c.formatVisitCount++
331: 	attrs := body.Attributes()
332: 	for name, attr := range attrs {
333: 		if len(inBlocks) == 1 && inBlocks[0] == "variable" && name == "type" {
334: 			cleanedExprTokens := c.formatTypeExpr(attr.Expr().BuildTokens(nil))
335: 			body.SetAttributeRaw(name, cleanedExprTokens)
336: 			continue
337: 		}
338: 		cleanedExprTokens := c.formatValueExpr(attr.Expr().BuildTokens(nil))
339: 		body.SetAttributeRaw(name, cleanedExprTokens)
340: 	}
341: 
342: 	blocks := body.Blocks()
343: 	for _, block := range blocks {
344: 		// Normalize the label formatting, removing any weird stuff like
345: 		// interleaved inline comments and using the idiomatic quoted
346: 		// label syntax.
347: 		block.SetLabels(block.Labels())
348: 
349: 		inBlocks := append(inBlocks, block.Type())
350: 		c.formatBody(block.Body(), inBlocks)
351: 	}
352: }

354: func (c *FmtCommand) formatValueExpr(tokens hclwrite.Tokens) hclwrite.Tokens {
355: 	c.lastValueExprLen = len(tokens)
356: 	c.formatVisitCount++
357: 	if len(tokens) < 5 {
358: 		// Can't possibly be a "${ ... }" sequence without at least enough
359: 		// tokens for the delimiters and one token inside them.
360: 		return tokens
361: 	}
362: 	oQuote := tokens[0]
363: 	oBrace := tokens[1]
364: 	cBrace := tokens[len(tokens)-2]
365: 	cQuote := tokens[len(tokens)-1]
366: 	if oQuote.Type != hclsyntax.TokenOQuote || oBrace.Type != hclsyntax.TokenTemplateInterp || cBrace.Type != hclsyntax.TokenTemplateSeqEnd || cQuote.Type != hclsyntax.TokenCQuote {
367: 		// Not an interpolation sequence at all, then.
368: 		return tokens
369: 	}
370: 
371: 	inside := tokens[2 : len(tokens)-2]
372: 
373: 	// We're only interested in sequences that are provable to be single
374: 	// interpolation sequences, which we'll determine by hunting inside
375: 	// the interior tokens for any other interpolation sequences. This is
376: 	// likely to produce false negatives sometimes, but that's better than
377: 	// false positives and we're mainly interested in catching the easy cases
378: 	// here.
379: 	quotes := 0
380: 	for _, token := range inside {
381: 		if token.Type == hclsyntax.TokenOQuote {
382: 			quotes++
383: 			continue
384: 		}
385: 		if token.Type == hclsyntax.TokenCQuote {
386: 			quotes--
387: 			continue
388: 		}
389: 		if quotes > 0 {
390: 			// Interpolation sequences inside nested quotes are okay, because
391: 			// they are part of a nested expression.
392: 			// "${foo("${bar}")}"
393: 			continue
394: 		}
395: 		if token.Type == hclsyntax.TokenTemplateInterp || token.Type == hclsyntax.TokenTemplateSeqEnd {
396: 			// We've found another template delimiter within our interior
397: 			// tokens, which suggests that we've found something like this:
398: 			// "${foo}${bar}"
399: 			// That isn't unwrappable, so we'll leave the whole expression alone.
400: 			return tokens
401: 		}
402: 		if token.Type == hclsyntax.TokenQuotedLit {
403: 			// If there's any literal characters in the outermost
404: 			// quoted sequence then it is not unwrappable.
405: 			return tokens
406: 		}
407: 	}
408: 
409: 	// If we got down here without an early return then this looks like
410: 	// an unwrappable sequence, but we'll trim any leading and trailing
411: 	// newlines that might result in an invalid result if we were to
412: 	// naively trim something like this:
413: 	// "${
414: 	//    foo
415: 	// }"
416: 	trimmed := c.trimNewlines(inside)
417: 
418: 	// Finally, we check if the unwrapped expression is on multiple lines. If
419: 	// so, we ensure that it is surrounded by parenthesis to make sure that it
420: 	// parses correctly after unwrapping. This may be redundant in some cases,
421: 	// but is required for at least multi-line ternary expressions.
422: 	isMultiLine := false
423: 	hasLeadingParen := false
424: 	hasTrailingParen := false
425: 	for i, token := range trimmed {
426: 		switch {
427: 		case i == 0 && token.Type == hclsyntax.TokenOParen:
428: 			hasLeadingParen = true
429: 		case token.Type == hclsyntax.TokenNewline:
430: 			isMultiLine = true
431: 		case i == len(trimmed)-1 && token.Type == hclsyntax.TokenCParen:
432: 			hasTrailingParen = true
433: 		}
434: 	}
435: 	if isMultiLine && !(hasLeadingParen && hasTrailingParen) {
436: 		wrapped := make(hclwrite.Tokens, 0, len(trimmed)+2)
437: 		wrapped = append(wrapped, &hclwrite.Token{
438: 			Type:  hclsyntax.TokenOParen,
439: 			Bytes: []byte("("),
440: 		})
441: 		wrapped = append(wrapped, trimmed...)
442: 		wrapped = append(wrapped, &hclwrite.Token{
443: 			Type:  hclsyntax.TokenCParen,
444: 			Bytes: []byte(")"),
445: 		})
446: 
447: 		return wrapped
448: 	}
449: 
450: 	return trimmed
451: }

453: func (c *FmtCommand) formatTypeExpr(tokens hclwrite.Tokens) hclwrite.Tokens {
454: 	c.lastValueExprLen = len(tokens)
455: 	c.formatVisitCount++
456: 	switch len(tokens) {
457: 	case 1:
458: 		kwTok := tokens[0]
459: 		if kwTok.Type != hclsyntax.TokenIdent {
460: 			// Not a single type keyword, then.
461: 			return tokens
462: 		}
463: 
464: 		// Collection types without an explicit element type mean
465: 		// the element type is "any", so we'll normalize that.
466: 		switch string(kwTok.Bytes) {
467: 		case "list", "map", "set":
468: 			return hclwrite.Tokens{
469: 				kwTok,
470: 				{
471: 					Type:  hclsyntax.TokenOParen,
472: 					Bytes: []byte("("),
473: 				},
474: 				{
475: 					Type:  hclsyntax.TokenIdent,
476: 					Bytes: []byte("any"),
477: 				},
478: 				{
479: 					Type:  hclsyntax.TokenCParen,
480: 					Bytes: []byte(")"),
481: 				},
482: 			}
483: 		default:
484: 			return tokens
485: 		}
486: 
487: 	case 3:
488: 		// A pre-0.12 legacy quoted string type, like "string".
489: 		oQuote := tokens[0]
490: 		strTok := tokens[1]
491: 		cQuote := tokens[2]
492: 		if oQuote.Type != hclsyntax.TokenOQuote || strTok.Type != hclsyntax.TokenQuotedLit || cQuote.Type != hclsyntax.TokenCQuote {
493: 			// Not a quoted string sequence, then.
494: 			return tokens
495: 		}
496: 
497: 		// Because this quoted syntax is from Terraform 0.11 and
498: 		// earlier, which didn't have the idea of "any" as an,
499: 		// element type, we use string as the default element
500: 		// type. That will avoid oddities if somehow the configuration
501: 		// was relying on numeric values being auto-converted to
502: 		// string, as 0.11 would do. This mimicks what terraform
503: 		// 0.12upgrade used to do, because we'd found real-world
504: 		// modules that were depending on the auto-stringing.)
505: 		switch string(strTok.Bytes) {
506: 		case "string":
507: 			return hclwrite.Tokens{
508: 				{
509: 					Type:  hclsyntax.TokenIdent,
510: 					Bytes: []byte("string"),
511: 				},
512: 			}
513: 		case "list":
514: 			return hclwrite.Tokens{
515: 				{
516: 					Type:  hclsyntax.TokenIdent,
517: 					Bytes: []byte("list"),
518: 				},
519: 				{
520: 					Type:  hclsyntax.TokenOParen,
521: 					Bytes: []byte("("),
522: 				},
523: 				{
524: 					Type:  hclsyntax.TokenIdent,
525: 					Bytes: []byte("string"),
526: 				},
527: 				{
528: 					Type:  hclsyntax.TokenCParen,
529: 					Bytes: []byte(")"),
530: 				},
531: 			}
532: 		case "map":
533: 			return hclwrite.Tokens{
534: 				{
535: 					Type:  hclsyntax.TokenIdent,
536: 					Bytes: []byte("map"),
537: 				},
538: 				{
539: 					Type:  hclsyntax.TokenOParen,
540: 					Bytes: []byte("("),
541: 				},
542: 				{
543: 					Type:  hclsyntax.TokenIdent,
544: 					Bytes: []byte("string"),
545: 				},
546: 				{
547: 					Type:  hclsyntax.TokenCParen,
548: 					Bytes: []byte(")"),
549: 				},
550: 			}
551: 		default:
552: 			// Something else we're not expecting, then.
553: 			return tokens
554: 		}
555: 	default:
556: 		return tokens
557: 	}
558: }

560: func (c *FmtCommand) trimNewlines(tokens hclwrite.Tokens) hclwrite.Tokens {
561: 	c.lastValueExprLen = len(tokens)
562: 	c.formatVisitCount++
563: 	if len(tokens) == 0 {
564: 		return nil
565: 	}
566: 	var start, end int
567: 	for start = 0; start < len(tokens); start++ {
568: 		if tokens[start].Type != hclsyntax.TokenNewline {
569: 			break
570: 		}
571: 	}
572: 	for end = len(tokens); end > 0; end-- {
573: 		if tokens[end-1].Type != hclsyntax.TokenNewline {
574: 			break
575: 		}
576: 	}
577: 	return tokens[start:end]
578: }

1268: 		diags = append(diags, traversalDiags...)
